So 'required' forces Gemini into ANY mode, meaning the model must always call a function and can never reply with plain text—so after a decline it just keeps calling tools instead of stopping. The fix is to switch to 'auto' mode, matching what the triage agent already uses, though I need to check the system prompt's refund-approval rule still holds under that setting.

I'll proceed with editing the file, replacing `toolChoice: 'required',` with `toolChoice: 'auto',` since that's the exact broken text causing the issue. No git repo to worry about, so I'll just make the edit directly.

I'll change it to `'auto'`, which triage already uses.

I'm checking that the system prompt really has no text-reply path after a decline, and that the toolChoice snippet and line-43 citation in answer.json match what I actually read.

Since I didn't run this live, I should note that caveat, and maybe suggest as an optional improvement adding an explicit system prompt instruction for handling declines.

The root cause was `toolChoice: 'required'` on `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts` (line 43). I changed it to `'auto'`, the same setting triage uses.

With `'required'`, the Gemini plugin sends function-calling mode `ANY`, so the model must call a tool on every turn. After the supervisor declines, it can't reply in text. It keeps calling `approveRefund` or `lookupOrder` until `maxTurns` runs out, which matches the failures in the report.

`tsc --noEmit` passes. I didn't run the refund flow end to end, since that needs a live Gemini API call, so the behavior change is verified from the plugin source rather than a live run. `answer.json` is written to the project root with the file, snippet, cause and evidence. `package.json` is unchanged.
